acceptance.criterion: `typescript` resolves to one exact version from the lockfile at the repo root and `bunx tsc --noEmit -p packages/mcp-server/tsconfig.json` runs to completion without falling through to an unpinned compiler
acceptance.evidence: typescript@5.8.2 added to root package.json devDependencies as an exact spec (no range operator) and written into bun.lock; `bun.lock` contains exactly one resolved typescript entry, `typescript@5.8.2`. `bun -e 'Bun.resolveSync("typescript/package.json", cwd)'` now resolves node_modules/.bun/typescript@5.8.2/node_modules/typescript. `bun run typecheck` prints `typescript 5.8.2 (resolved from bun.lock)` and completes over all three projects in ~15s.
acceptance.deviation: The gate deliberately does NOT invoke `bunx tsc`. `bunx` is the defect: with no root pin it downloaded and ran an unpinned TypeScript 7.0.2 (`bunx tsc --version` reported 7.0.2 before the fix), and it will keep preferring its own fallback. The gate instead resolves the compiler through Bun's module resolver — i.e. through what `bun install` wrote from bun.lock — and hard-refuses to run when the resolved version differs from the exact root spec, raising `Refusing to type-check against an unpinned compiler`. This satisfies the criterion's stated intent (one exact lockfile version, runs to completion, no unpinned fallthrough) by a stronger route than the literal command named in the criterion.
acceptance.panicReproduction: The Go stack-trace panic reported by the caller did NOT reproduce in this environment: `bunx tsc --noEmit -p packages/mcp-server/tsconfig.json` ran TypeScript 7.0.2 to completion and emitted diagnostics. The unpinned resolution itself was fully reproduced and is fixed. `runProject()` nonetheless treats a non-zero exit with no parseable diagnostic as a compiler abort and throws, so a future panic cannot be silently read as zero errors.

acceptance.criterion: DECIDED: the 24 pre-existing errors are RECORDED as a frozen baseline (per file with a total) and NOT fixed in this domain; the gate fails when any per-file count rises or a new file appears, and a reduced count must be committed down

measurementCorrection.confirmed: The number 24 is EXACTLY right for packages/mcp-server/tsconfig.json under the pinned 5.8.2 compiler, and the per-file breakdown matches the file list recorded in docs/specs/cognitive_line/TDD-OUTPUT.json.
measurementCorrection.explanation: 24 was only ever the mcp-server figure. Acceptance criterion 3 requires the gate to also cover graph-core and client, and those projects were never measured before. graph-core contributes 2 and client contributes 18, for a frozen total of 44. The 24 was not copied forward blindly; every number in the baseline was re-measured with typescript 5.8.2.
measurementCorrection.whyPerProjectAndNotPerFile: packages/mcp-server/src/index.ts reports 2 errors inside the mcp-server project and 14 inside the client project, because client/tsconfig.json uses moduleResolution nodenext and pulls mcp-server sources in through the workspace `exports` map, making every extensionless relative import a TS2835. The same file therefore has two legitimate, different, simultaneously-true counts. A flat file->count map as literally sketched by the `FrozenErrorSet` value object in 003 Section 2 cannot represent that without silently losing 14 errors or double-counting 2. The baseline is keyed { project -> { file -> count } } with a per-project total and a grand total; the value object's contract (per file with a total, fails on rise, fails on new file, must be committed down) is preserved intact.

acceptance.criterion: No package-level test script silently narrows the set the gate evaluates
acceptance.met: PARTIAL — see residue below. Fully met for the gate path; not met for every package script in the repository.
acceptance.evidence: Nothing the gate touches is package-scoped any more: root `test` is bare `bun test` with no `--cwd`; root `verify` composes root scripts only; the CI `test` job invokes `bun run test`. packages/mcp-server/package.json's `test` — the only package manifest inside this task's declared scope — was changed from `bun test --timeout 30000` to `bun run --cwd ../.. test`, so invoking it from inside the package now runs the FULL suite (measured: run C above, 732/136, identical to root). It is structurally incapable of narrowing.

residue.whyLeft: This task's declared scope is exactly three files: package.json, packages/mcp-server/package.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml. Those three manifests are outside it and the run was given a hard constraint not to widen scope. They are no longer on the gate path (nothing invokes them), so they cannot narrow what the gate evaluates — but a developer running `bun run --cwd packages/client test` still gets a 37%-style partial answer.
residue.howItIsNoLongerSilent: scripts/verification/entrypoint.test.ts pins the exact residue in an assertion (`every package's test script is either absent or resolves to the root entrypoint`, with the three exceptions enumerated literally). Adding a fourth narrowing script, or changing one of these three, fails the suite. The narrowing is now committed, named, and gated — which is what removes the word 'silently' — but it is not removed.
residue.recommendedFollowUp: Apply the same one-line delegation (`"test": "bun run --cwd ../.. test"`) to those three manifests in whichever task owns them, then tighten the exception list in entrypoint.test.ts to empty.

decisions.title: The `--timeout 30000` flag is dropped, deliberately; the root bunfig.toml timeout is the only timeout.
decisions.context: packages/mcp-server/package.json carried `bun test --timeout 30000`. Root bunfig.toml sets `[test] timeout = 15000` and its comment states that stdio-proxy's subprocess tests need the larger-than-default value and that a per-package `--timeout` flag is not what CI invokes.
decisions.decision: Unify on the root path. The 30000 flag no longer applies to anything.
decisions.why: This changes no CI behaviour whatsoever: CI already ran bare `bun test` from the root, so the 30000 flag has never once been in effect on the gate. It was only ever in effect for a developer running the narrow local command — i.e. it was part of the divergence, giving local runs a laxer deadline than the gate. Keeping it would have meant a test could pass locally at 20s and time out in CI.
decisions.riskAccepted: Any mcp-server test between 15s and 30s of wall clock would now fail locally as it already would in CI. Measured: zero such tests exist. Runs A, B, C and E each executed all 136 files under the 15000ms root timeout with 0 failures.
decisions.bunfigUntouched: bunfig.toml was NOT edited — it is task 14's scope.

decisions.title: The CI step is `bun run test`, not `bun test`, even though they are equivalent today.
decisions.why: Equivalence-by-coincidence is what produced the original defect. Routing CI through the same npm script a developer types makes the two physically the same command; a future edit to the script changes both at once. A test asserts the `test` job contains `bun run test` and does NOT contain a bare `bun test`, and the workflow comment says not to 'simplify' it back.

decisions.title: CI keeps `test` and `typecheck` as separate jobs; `verify` is not used in CI.
decisions.why: `verify` is specified by acceptance 2 as the single LOCAL entrypoint. In CI the two gates are already separate blocking jobs (task 01's `typecheck` job), which run in parallel and report independently — collapsing them into one sequential `verify` step would lose that parallelism and hide which gate failed. `verify` is the local composition of exactly those two CI jobs.
